replies.bodyText: That's because we don't access the configuration value through the logFileMaxSize ConfigurationOption instance. That would require the configuration registry to be initialized already. However, the registry initializes logging. In order to break up the cyclic dependency and to not accidentally initialize logging before we had the chance to configure the logging, we manually resolve these options.

timeline.body:
there is some commented code, probably leftovers.

Also, not really sure about the wording, something like `agent keeps one history file, thus the amount of storage used by agent logs will be equal to twice this value`.

I feel that we could make this less confusing by using a value that is half of the configured value.
IMHO it provides the following advantages:
- users expect a limit to be enforced, and using twice the configured value would be seen as a defect, even if it's documented
- it's unlikely that anyone will complain about the agent using less storage than expected, nobody wants a full hard drive
- we could still document that this limit is shared between the two copies of the log file when using log shipping feature.

replies.bodyText:
there is some commented code, probably leftovers

This is intentionally left in as it will be needed when we support shipping logs.

I feel that we could make this less confusing by using a value that is half of the configured value.

The reason why I did it this way is that log_file_max_size also determines how much is buffered on disk before data is deleted. When shipping logs, it basically determines how much data can be buffered without data loss while the APM Server is down. So they might expect that we always buffer at least log_file_max_size. We can only guarantee that, if both the primary and the history log file have the max size of log_file_max_size.
replies.author: felixbarny

replies.bodyText: Then, probably removing the 'max' from the configuration would remove any expectation to be the actual max disk usage by the agent. for example if we name it log_file_buffer_size and then document that disk usage is at most equal to twice this value.
replies.author: SylvainJuge

timeline.body: why do we need to poll just after stop is requested ?
timeline.bodyText: why do we need to poll just after stop is requested ?
timeline.bodyHTML: why do we need to poll just after stop is requested ?
timeline.author: SylvainJuge

replies.bodyText:
That's because we want to make sure we have sent everything in the file and don't immediately stop sending when shutting down. We should also attempt to send logs emitted during the shutdown. But the timeout provided to the stop method makes sure we don't block indefinitely.
This part is still very much POC and WIP which is why there's also not a lot of docs. Part of it is specified in elastic/apm#252 but it lacks some details atm.
Again, this code is not active by default and can only be activated through an internal option.
replies.author: felixbarny
